title: Torque (Moment of Force)

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 11 — System of Particles and Rotational Motion

domain: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
explanation: Torque measures the turning effect of a force about a chosen axis/point, equal to the cross product of the position vector r (from axis to point of force application) and the force F. Magnitude is rF sinθ, maximum when the force is applied perpendicular to r (θ = 90°) and zero when force is applied along r (θ = 0°, no turning effect at all). Direction is given by the right-hand rule, perpendicular to both r and F.

variables.meaning: Position vector from axis to point of force application

workedExample.scenario: A 10 N force is applied perpendicular to a 0.3 m wrench handle.

commonMistakes: Applying force along the position vector (θ = 0°) and expecting a non-zero torque — this produces zero turning effect, regardless of force magnitude.
Forgetting torque units (N·m) look dimensionally like energy (J) but are conceptually different — never add or equate the two directly.
genZNote: Torque's whole vibe: it's not the force, it's the distance from the axis that does the real work.
